claim: In the new list view (promRule only, no ruler rule) the "Silence notifications" menu item is shown but clicking it does nothing, because the drawer is gated on rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) and rule is now undefined.
body:
## [ISSUE] "Silence notifications" is offered in the list view but the drawer can never open

**Severity:** HIGH — a visible, enabled action silently does nothing for every Grafana-managed alerting rule in the new list view.

### The Problem

`GrafanaRuleListItem` now renders `<RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule} groupIdentifier={groupIdentifier} compact />` with no `rule` prop. `AlertRuleMenu` computes `canSilence` as `(ruler) || (grafanaSilenceSupported && grafanaSilenceAllowed)`, and `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` returns `[silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]` for prom rules, so the menu item is rendered. Clicking it calls `handleSilence` -> `setShowSilenceDrawer(true)`, but the drawer is rendered only when:

```tsx
{rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer && (
  <SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer rulerRule={rule} onClose={() => setShowSilenceDrawer(false)} />
)}
```

`rule` is `undefined` here, so the condition is always false.

### Theory / Proof

- `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:48` passes only `promRule`.
- `AlertRuleMenu.tsx:124-130` renders the Silence item whenever `canSilence` is true.
- `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:104` requires a ruler rule to mount the drawer.
- The new test `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx` ("should render correct menu actions") asserts the silence item exists but never clicks it, so the dead action is not caught.

### What happens today vs. what will break

Before this PR every list item had a ruler rule, so the drawer opened. After it, the list view has no ruler rule, so the button stays visible and clicking it has no effect and shows no error.

### Research

`SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` only needs the rule UID to pre-fill the `__alert_rule_uid__` matcher. The prom DTO already carries `uid`, so the ruler DTO is not required.

### Recommendation

Let the drawer accept a rule UID (or a prom rule) and render it from either source:

```tsx
const silenceRuleUid = rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)
  ? rule.grafana_alert.uid
  : prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(promRule)
    ? promRule.uid
    : undefined;

{silenceRuleUid && showSilenceDrawer && (
  <SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer ruleUid={silenceRuleUid} onClose={() => setShowSilenceDrawer(false)} />
)}
```

Also add a test that clicks the menu item and asserts the drawer opens.

claim: Pause and Delete are still gated on rulerRule in AlertRuleMenu, so the new prom-only list view can never show them even though useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities computes grafanaPauseAbility/grafanaDeleteAbility; the new test locks in only 4 menu items.
body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] Pause and Delete disappear from the new list view; the prom-based abilities for them are computed but unused

**Severity:** MEDIUM — users with edit/delete permissions lose the Pause/Resume and Delete actions from the rule list.

### The Problem

The PR adds `grafanaPauseAbility` and `grafanaDeleteAbility` and ORs them into `canPause`/`canDelete`, but rendering still requires a ruler rule:

```tsx
{canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && groupIdentifier.groupOrigin === 'grafana' && (
  <MenuItemPauseRule rule={rulerRule} ... />
)}
...
{canDelete && rulerRule && ( ... handleDelete(rulerRule, groupIdentifier) ... )}
```

The list view (`GrafanaRuleListItem`) now passes only `promRule`, so `rulerRule` is always `undefined` and neither item renders, whatever the permissions.

### Theory / Proof

- `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:48` passes no `rule`, and `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:95` forwards `rulerRule={rule}` (undefined).
- `AlertRuleMenu.tsx:123` and `:165` check `rulerRule`.
- The new test `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx` grants `AlertingRuleUpdate`/`AlertingRuleDelete` and still asserts `menuItems.length).toBe(4)` (silence, copy link, duplicate, export). That confirms Pause and Delete are gone even for fully privileged users.

### What happens today vs. what will break

Before: list items had ruler rules, so Pause and Delete appeared. After: they are silently removed, and the prom-side ability plumbing for them is dead code.

### Research

`MenuItemPauseRule` and `useDeleteModal` both work from a rule UID plus group identifier. The ruler DTO is fetched only to rebuild the group for the update call. That can be done lazily on click (fetch the ruler group, then mutate), which keeps the ruler API off the list page's initial render.

### Recommendation

Either make the prom path fully functional or remove the dead abilities. For example:

```tsx
{canPause && groupIdentifier.groupOrigin === 'grafana' && (rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) || prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule)) && (
  <MenuItemPauseRule ruleUid={rulerRule?.grafana_alert.uid ?? promRule.uid} groupIdentifier={groupIdentifier} onPauseChange={onPauseChange} />
)}
```

Have `MenuItemPauseRule` and the delete handler fetch the ruler group on demand. Update the test to expect Pause and Delete when the permissions are granted.

claim: useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities which hard-codes isFederated=false, dropping the previous isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check so Mimir federated rule groups become editable/deletable in the legacy list and details UI.

useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities uses prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule for ModifyExport/Pause/Restore/DeletePermanently, whereas the ruler version used grafana.rule (alerting + recording), so Grafana recording rules lose Export (and the other actions) in the list view.
body:
## [ISSUE] Grafana recording rules lose Export (and Pause/Restore/DeletePermanently) under the prom-based abilities

**Severity:** LOW — a feature regression for recording rules in the new list view.

### The Problem

```ts
// All GrafanaPromRuleDTO rules are Grafana-managed by definition
const isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule);
...
[AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport]: [isAlertingRule, exportAllowed],
[AlertRuleAction.Pause]: [MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isAlertingRule, ...],
```

The ruler equivalent uses `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule = rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which is true for both alerting and recording rules. The comment describes "Grafana-managed" but the code checks "alerting", so the behaviour differs.

### Theory / Proof

`prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule` (`utils/rules.ts:134`) excludes `isGrafanaPromRecordingRule`. In the list view only the prom path is active, because `rulerRule` is undefined. As a result `canExport` is false for Grafana recording rules and the Export menu item disappears. The same rules still show Export on the rule detail page, where the ruler path is ORed in.

### What happens today vs. what will break

Export (and, once #2 is fixed, Pause) is missing for recording rules in the list but present on the detail page, so the two views disagree.

### Recommendation

Use the Grafana-rule predicate for the actions that apply to both rule types, and keep the alerting-only check for Silence:

```ts
const isGrafanaManagedRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule);
const isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule);
...
[AlertRuleAction.Silence]: [silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule],
[AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport]: [isGrafanaManagedRule, exportAllowed],
[AlertRuleAction.Pause]: [MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isGrafanaManagedRule, isEditable ?? false],
[AlertRuleAction.Restore]: [MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isGrafanaManagedRule, isEditable ?? false],
[AlertRuleAction.DeletePermanently]: [MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isGrafanaManagedRule, (isRemovable && isAdmin()) ?? false],
```

claim: The rewritten GrafanaRuleListItem drops the returnTo query param (createReturnTo()) from the rule view link, so navigating from the list to a rule and back loses the current list filters/search, unlike the removed implementation and DataSourceRuleListItem.
body:
## [ISSUE] Rule view link no longer carries `returnTo`

**Severity:** LOW — a UX regression: after opening a rule from a filtered list, "back" does not return to the filtered list.

### The Problem

Removed code (`GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx`):
```tsx
const returnTo = createReturnTo();
href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo }),
```
New code:
```tsx
href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`),
```

### Theory / Proof

`DataSourceRuleListItem.tsx:36-42` still builds its link with `createReturnTo()`, so data source rules and Grafana rules now behave differently in the same list. The rule viewer uses `returnTo` to go back to the list with the original filter and search query string.

### What happens today vs. what will break

A user filters the list (for example `?search=state:firing`), opens a Grafana rule, and clicks back or the breadcrumb. They land on the unfiltered list. Data source rules keep the filter.

### Recommendation

```tsx
import { createReturnTo } from '../hooks/useReturnTo';
...
const returnTo = createReturnTo();
...
href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo }),
```
